alt: A thin, dark soil lies directly over jointed granite on Île de Berder, Brittany.
caption: Rankosol over granite on Île de Berder, France. A shallow organic-rich surface over non-calcareous bedrock illustrates a ranker; horizons are real field layers, not a template.

credit: Samuel Rios / USDA NRCS · public domain · via Wikimedia Commons · resized
alt: A deep reddish Nipe-series soil profile with a measuring tape in Puerto Rico.
caption: USDA NRCS Nipe-series profile at Cerro Las Mesas, Puerto Rico, January 2002. Classified as Typic Acrudox, this Oxisol formed through deep weathering of iron-rich parent material.

alt: A Puerto Rican soil profile has a dark surface above pale carbonate-rich subsoil, with a depth scale.
caption: Aridic Calciustoll near Ponce, Puerto Rico: a Mollisol with a roughly 30 cm mollic surface over a calcic horizon. Its parent material includes colluvium and weathered limestone.

alt: A rocky opening in grassy limestone terrain at Stream Passage Pot in the Gaping Gill cave system.
caption: Stream Passage Pot, Ingleborough, North Yorkshire. This entrance belongs to the Gaping Gill karst drainage system, where surface water enters underground passages.

alt: White chalk cliffs, offshore remnants and a wave-cut base near the Pinnacles in Purbeck.
caption: The Pinnacles coast, Purbeck, Dorset. Erosion leaves isolated stacks and lower remnants called stumps beside the retreating chalk cliffs.

alt: NOAA seafloor relief map around Puerto Rico identifies the deep Puerto Rico Trench and nearby plate boundary.
caption: NOAA bathymetric visualisation of the Puerto Rico region. A trench is an elongated seafloor depression associated here with a complex convergent plate boundary; vertical relief is exaggerated in this perspective.

credit: Carol M. Highsmith · The Jon B. Lovelace Collection of California Photographs in Carol M. Highsmith's America Project, Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division · public domain · resized
alt: Aerial view of the San Andreas Fault cutting across dry hills in California.
caption: San Andreas Fault in California's Sierra Madre Mountains. The fault accommodates mainly horizontal motion between the Pacific and North American plates.

alt: Sentinel-6 sea-surface height anomaly map shows lower-than-average levels across the central and eastern equatorial Pacific.
caption: Sentinel-6, 13 January 2025. Lower sea-surface heights accompanied La Niña's cooler equatorial waters. Colours show height anomalies, not sea-surface temperature; seasonal cycles and long-term trends were removed.
